title: Open-source CLI, docs site with several pages
opening: I need a docs site for my CLI tool
persona: Yusuf Kaya, maintainer of a small open-source command-line tool. Precise, technical, answers fully but briefly.
facts: The tool is tidyrun, a CLI that runs a project's scripts in a clean temporary copy so they cannot touch the working tree.
Install with: npm install -g tidyrun. Requires Node 20 or later.
Commands: tidyrun <script>, tidyrun --keep, tidyrun --diff, tidyrun init.
The one thing a visitor should do is install it and run it once on their own project.
Readers are developers who were bitten by a script that changed files it should not have.
Wants a home page, an install page, a commands reference, and a FAQ that answers the three questions people actually open issues about.
No logo, no domain; GitHub Pages is fine.
Does not want a blog, analytics, or a newsletter.
taste: If asked for a material or object with the right colour: a terminal on a dim screen is too obvious, so: the green of an old engineering ledger and black ink. Likes dense, well-organised reference pages. Accepts light or dark.

# tidyrun

Run your project's scripts in a clean temporary copy so they cannot touch your working tree.

## Install
npm install -g tidyrun (Node 20+)

## Commands
- tidyrun <script>: run a package.json script in a temp copy
- tidyrun --keep: keep the temp copy for inspection
- tidyrun --diff: show what the script would have changed
- tidyrun init: write a .tidyrunrc with defaults

## Common issues
1. Scripts that need env files: add them to .tidyrunrc include.
2. Large node_modules: tidyrun links them instead of copying.
3. Windows paths: use forward slashes in .tidyrunrc.
